Amazon Wish Lists
Many families ask how they can support the school in place of individual staff gifts. Each year group has created an Amazon Wish List featuring items chosen specifically for their class.
If you would like to support the children in this way, please take a look at the lists. If there is something you’d like to purchase, simply order it as you would anything else on Amazon. Your gift will be delivered directly to the school and marked for the attention of the relevant teacher.
Thank you for your kindness and support — it is truly appreciated.

Whole School Wishlist
The Amazon Wish Lists will be regularly updated by staff and are an easy and safe way to support our school to continue to provide a rich, wide-ranging curriculum and a high standard of education.
We are always grateful for donations to enhance the learning of our children. You can also contribute by joining/supporting the PTA, volunteering in school and donating items such as pre-loved uniform and good as new resources and equipment. Thank you in advance for your generosity.
*Please do not make any orders during the school holidays as there is not always someone to receive deliveries and items may go missing.

pageCache.pageTitle: Herstmonceux Church of England Primary School - School Meals
pageCache.text:
School Meals
Children are offered a range of tasty and healthy school meals that are prepared freshly, on site every day by Chartwells. Lunch consists of a main meal (hot and cold with vegetarian options), pudding and water or milk. School meals are booked and paid for via ParentPay.
School meals are free of charge to all Infant children (from Reception to Year 2, inclusive). For more information on Universal Infant Free School Meals (UIFSM) please view the Government webpage.
View the current Chartwells menu here.
Free School Meals
Your child may be entitled to Free School Meals (FSM) if you as parents receive one or more qualifying benefits. It is vital that all parents / carers who are entitled to these benefits apply for FSM even in Years R, 1 and 2 when you do not pay for school meals. If you do qualify, the school will receive extra funding to support your child’s learning in school.
You can apply for Free School Meals via this link.
Please refer to our Pupil Premium page for information about how this additional funding has been spent to help your children.
Fruit and Milk
EYFS and KS1 children benefit from the national free fruit and vegetables scheme and are provided with this on a daily basis to eat at break time. KS2 children are encouraged to bring in a healthy fruit or veg snack for morning break.
Early Years children are also entitled to a free serving of milk up until their fifth birthday, which parents need to sign up to, via Cool Milk.
Kindly note that our school is nut free due to pupils having anaphylactic allergies.

School Uniform
We believe that school uniform is practical and helps to give the school a special identity. We ask for your co-operation in providing the school uniform for your child and ensuring that it is worn.
The uniform consists of:
You can order embroidered items online via one of the companies we use -
Your school uniform : www.yourschooluniform.com
My Clothing: www.myclothing.com
Brigade Clothing: www.brigade.uk.com
Order deadline for Brigade • Parents Direct (delivery to home): Order by Friday 17th July for delivery to home before the start of term.
Please ensure all items of uniform, including drinks bottles (which should only contain water), lunch boxes and bags are clearly labelled with your child’s name – this allows quick return of all lost items. If you need any help at all in relation to uniform please contact the school office and we will be more than happy to help you.
Label your school clothing and items, and raise funds for our school at the same time! Click here to order Stikins name labels and raise money for the school. We receive 30% commission to help fund activities in school. Use our school code 9470.
Navy blue sweatshirt/cardigan with yellow school logo
Yellow polo shirt with blue school logo
Grey trousers/shorts/pinafore dress/skirt
Blue gingham summer school dress (optional)
Navy fleece with school logo (optional)
Black school shoes (not trainers)
Grey or navy socks/tights (not leggings)
White t-shirt with blue school logo
Navy shorts
Plimsolls or trainers
Long hair should be tied back
School Bags
We provide a new book bag, free of charge, to our reception class. We do ask that you use these as space is limited in the cloakroom and rucksacks are too bulky. As your child moves up the school then they are welcome to pick their own design of rucksack for transporting their belongings to and from school.
School Clothes
If your child needs to have their clothes changed at school for any reason, please wash and return the borrowed clothes to school as soon as possible.

SIAMS inspection focuses on the impact of the Church school's Christian vision on pupils and adults. This involves looking at the school’s Christian vision, the provision the school makes because of this vision and how effective this provision is in enabling all pupils to flourish. Pupil Premium
Pupil premium is funding to improve education outcomes for disadvantaged pupils in schools in England. Evidence shows that disadvantaged children generally face additional challenges in reaching their potential at school and often do not perform as well as other pupils.
Background
Introduced in 2011, the Pupil Premium Grant (PPG) is a sum of money given to schools each year by the Government to improve the attainment of disadvantaged children.
This is based on research showing that children from low income families perform less well at school than their peers. Often, children who are entitled to pupil premium face challenges such as poor language and communication skills, lack of confidence and issues with attendance and punctuality. The pupil premium is intended to directly benefit the children who are eligible, helping to narrow the gap between them and their classmates.
Pupil Premium Grant (PPG) is additional funding to raise the attainment of disadvantaged pupils. It is based on the number of pupils:
We receive a certain amount of money per child to help us in our whole school aims of providing an outstanding education that includes the right opportunities for children to flourish.
We are required to produce a report every year saying how we are spending the money and what impact it has had, this is called the Pupil Premium Strategy report. Our ultimate aim is to 'close the gap' between the least and most advantaged children as well as making sure that self-esteem and well-being remain high.
At the beginning of each year parents of children in receipt of Pupil Premium can make uniform requests for a logoed sweatshirt/cardigan, a logoed PE top and a pair of school shoes. These requests should be make direct to the school office.
Monitoring & Evaluation
The school’s evaluation of its own performance is rigorous. Tracking of progress over time for each pupil is thorough and facilitates timely and appropriate intervention.

Special Educational Needs
Key Contacts
Our school SENCo is Kally Livingston (klivingston@sussexspires.co.uk)
Our SENCo Assistant is: Jane Volker
Our SEND Offer
Herstmonceux Church of England Primary is a fully inclusive school who ensures that all pupils achieve their potential personally, socially, emotionally, physically and educationally.
Our SEN information report lets you understand how we support pupils with special educational needs and disabilities.
We consult with pupils and their families on our local offer by meeting with parents regularly through SEN reviews, parents’ evenings and informal meetings, these can be prompted by parents, teachers or external professionals.
Children are identified as having a special educational need when their level of progress has become a cause for concern. Interventions are quickly put in place to cater for individual needs.
If your child is placed on the SEN register at school you will be contacted and a meeting arranged between you and your child’s class teacher. At this meeting your views about your child’s education, strengths, additional needs and what you feel works best for them will be discussed and included in the plan as will your child’s views. This is so you know exactly what support your child will be receiving in school and how long for, also how we expect this support to help them.
SEN Information
Herstmonceux SEN Information Report
ESCC Special Educational Needs in Schools Pros
Sussex Spires SEN policy
The other people / agencies and teams providing services to children with a special educational need / disability in school include:
We will work in partnership with other education providers to ensure that pupils make a successful transition to the next stages of their learning, through careful and coordinated planning of the transition. We provide scheduled transition days to the local secondary school and further visits for vulnerable children, we liaise with staff, including form teachers and SENCOs of the transitional schools. Should children need to transfer to specialist provision; a transition plan will be put in place.
Behaviour and anti-bullying policies are regularly reviewed with a focus on how they affect pupils’ with special educational needs or disabilities.
Other useful documents such as our Special Educational Needs and Inclusion Policy are also available in the policies section of the website.
The school’s self-evaluation process will look at teaching and learning for pupils with special educational needs and disabilities.
All school-related activities are evaluated in terms of their benefit to the learning and inclusion of pupils with special educational needs and disabilities.
